comments.author: @Me__Myself__and__I
comments.text:
On the topic of a post-labor economy / UBI there is something many are missing.  The economy doesn't need to keep working.  Corporations don't need to continue to exist.  Good don't need to continue being made and sold.  Everything we CURRENTLY u derstand about evonomics goes out the window and no longer applies once human labor no longer has value because everything is automated.

Consider the currently existing wealth inequality.  The most wealthy are a tiny fraction of the population but possess the majority of the wealth.  AI and robots will be owned and co trolled by those same ultra wealthy, much further extending the wealth inequality.  The ultra wealthy also own/control large amounts of land and natural resources.

If all human labor is replaced by automation, why do the billionaires need to care anythi g at all about 99.99% of the population (the non-wealthy)?  They literally don't need them for ANYTHING.  They don't need to keep selling them things.  The ultra wealthy can trade amongst themselves for AI, robots, power, land and natural resources.  Automation can design and build anything they desire.  They will live 100x more lavishly than now, with no need or concern for common people.

Don't expect ultra wealthy, greedy, control freaks to give up 90%+ their wealth out of the kindness of their hearjs just so that 99.99% of humanity doesn't starve to death.  Note they will also control or have acces to all the military AI/robotics systems to defend themselves.  Many of not most have doomsday bunkers in remote areas/islands.

The curre t path will not be good for humanity.  If humans survive ASI and manage to retain control the only humans remaini g will likely be the worst of us.

comments.author: @hanskarlsson3778
comments.text: I'm afraid Shapiro's "Banks will save the day for America" has virtually no support among leading economic thinkers on the future of the US economy. While David Shapiro's post-labor economics framework offers an innovative perspective on automation challenges, it lacks support from leading academic economists and policy researchers. The academic consensus suggests that banking institutions are more likely to capture benefits from technological change than to serve as architects of equitable distribution. Expert alternatives focus on institutional, political, and regulatory reforms that would constrain financial power rather than rely on it for economic transformation. Personally, I am pessimistic this will not happen in the US. The country is on the descent into an even crueler, more unequal and unfair place than it is today.

In a world where UBI (Universal Basic Income) becomes necessary, the inevitability of justifying your existence becomes relevant. I.e., what do you contribute if you don't produce? What 'can' you contribute if the majority of production is automated? Take this logic and expand it a bit, and you are quickly facing a situation where the sheer number of humans on the planet becomes a consequential factor. That, of course, leads to various forms of eugenics.
When Klaus Schwab and the WEF thought the slogan, "You will own nothing, and like it" was a great idea, how do you think they arrived at that sentiment?  Without some form of UBI it is impossible.  Now add to that the knowledge that if 'you' don't own anything then 'who' does?  Only a fool doesn't think that someone, somewhere, isn't making decisions for you and without your consent.  Oh sure, those people may entertain and placate the general public with the facade of democracy, but it will most assuredly be fascism in the truest sense.

At the risk of losing anyone who has made it this far, there's a reality one must face whenever you start down the rabbit hole of a fully orchestrated economic and social framework: Who is calling the shots? The obvious answer is, of course, humans (but it can now be assumed it will be humans assisted by powerful AI systems). If anyone honestly answers the question, 'Do you trust your government?' they will say, 'No'; and ironically, that same person will most likely accept the subtle chains of a UBI-type system.  At the very heart of all systems that seek to establish equality and equity lies the sinful heart of mankind.  No institution can purify the heart, but Jesus can. He alone changes people from the inside out.  I humbly implore you to seek Him without allowing prejudice to cloud your judgement.
